raw_response:
I’m still doing cotton on all 4.1 mu this year. At my age, and with only one person in the house, I won’t chase anything too fancy. Cotton is what I know, and on this small area I can still manage it myself if the weather is normal. Last year the fields that were sown on time and got enough base fertilizer held better, so this year I’ll still plant in mid to late April, use a local hybrid cotton seed, put most of the fertilizer in early, and then add a little more when the plants start setting squares if they look weak. Well water costs money, so I won’t irrigate too many times, but I also don’t dare let the seedlings suffer dry stress. I’d rather spend a bit on two irrigations than lose stand and regret it later. For pests, cotton cannot be careless, especially aphids and bollworm if they come. I won’t spray blindly every time, but if I see pressure starting, I will spray quickly because on such a small farm one bad patch hurts a lot.

Because I farm only 4.1 mu and have limited cash and labor, my plan is to keep it steady, not maximize yield on paper. I’ll do normal tillage before sowing, use plastic mulch if locally available and affordable, keep fertilizer at a moderate level, and rely on my own labor for almost everything. If input prices rise too much, the first thing I cut back is not seed or the first fertilizer, but extra topdressing and unnecessary sprays.
